episodes.182890: An upper level low moved through northeast Montana during the evening and nighttime hours.  This feature generated strong to severe thunderstorms, with strong winds being the main hazard.
episodes.183166: A storm moving offshore produced a strong wind gust along the Martin County coast.
episodes.183419: Lifting up out of the Big Bend of Florida, Hurricane Idalia weakened to a Tropical Storm as it moved out of southeastern Georgia. The tropical system then moved northeast along the coastal plain of South Carolina. This system produced scattered tree damage, some  flooding and one confirmed tornado.
episodes.184034: A deep trough moving into the Pacific Coast and a high pressure center east of Arizona brought a strong and moist southerly flow over Arizona. This brought scattered showers and thunderstorms over the high terrain with local heavy rain and hail.
episodes.184123: The El Yunque streamer developed during the late morning and early afternoon hours on the 31st of August. Up to 3 inches of rain fell across the northeastern municipalities. This caused flooding over the San Juan metro area.
episodes.184477: An upper level disturbance moved across the Billings Forecast Area during the afternoon and evening hours of the 30th which resulted in numerous thunderstorms to develop. In addition, temperature/dewpoint spreads were high. As a result, these thunderstorms produced mainly severe wind gusts.
episodes.184733: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved southwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Large hail, severe wind gusts, and localized flash flooding occurred on the east side of Tucson.
episodes.184772: Tropical Storm Idalia moved northeast across southeast North Carolina bringing flooding from heavy rain and storm surge, a few tropical storm force wind gusts and tornadoes late August 30 into August 31. Previously the storm was a Category 4 hurricane. weakening to Category 3 as it made landfall near Perry, Florida. Locally all sustained tropical storm force winds remained offshore.
episodes.184773: Tropical Storm Idalia moved northeast across northeast South Carolina bringing flooding from heavy rain and storm surge, a few tropical storm force wind gusts and tornadoes late August 30 into August 31. Previously the storm was a Category 4 hurricane. weakening to Category 3 as it made landfall near Perry, Florida. Locally all sustained tropical storm force winds remained offshore.
episodes.184850: A monsoon trough extended into the western waters of Guam and up and through Saipan.|Locally heavy showers developed within the trough and then moved over Guam during the afternoon hours of August 31st, causing flash flooding across the central portion of Guam.
episodes.184897: Thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a very slow moving warm front. Instability and deep-layer shear were marginal, but strong enough for severe weather to develop. Hail was the main concern in the first few severe storms that developed, with golf ball size hail reported at Dickinson in Stark County, and Arnegard in McKenzie County. The main threat then gradually switched towards wind later in the episode. The strongest reported wind gust was 62 mph north of Grenora, in Divide County.
episodes.184947: A push of monsoon moisture, which continued into September, fueled scattered thunderstorms over southeast California. One produced damaging winds.
episodes.185107: Idalia developed near the Yucatan Channel on August 27th and meandered around for a couple of days before moving into the Gulf of Mexico on August 29th. Idalia rapidly intensified into a major hurricane before making landfall in the Florida Big Bend area as a category 3 hurricane with sustained winds near 125 mph. Idalia then continued northeast through the Southeast U.S., eventually moving off the coast of South Carolina on August 31st as a tropical storm. Idalia then turned east and passed just south of Eastern NC before eventually moving on towards Bermuda.||Across Eastern NC, the biggest impacts from Idalia came from water. Across the northern half of Eastern NC, 2-4 of rain was common, with 5-10 common across the southern half of Eastern NC, closer to Idalia's path. Where the heaviest rain fell, there were numerous roads closed due to flash flooding. The heavy rainfall also forced the closure of campgrounds in Dare County. In Onslow County, several roads were washed out, and led to the development of sinkholes.||In addition to the rainfall impacts, there were also some impacts due to storm surge. Water levels reached as high as 4 feet above ground level, especially in Carteret County, with impacts focused in Downeast, Great Neck Creek, and Back Creek.||Tropical storm force winds were primarily felt across the southern half of Eastern NC, where gusts peaked in the 40 to 60 mph range, with a few higher gusts. This caused some tree damage and power outages.
episodes.185144: Idalia first developed into a tropical depression across the western Caribbean Sea near the Yucatan Peninsula on August 26th before slowly gaining strength and becoming a tropical storm on August 27th. The storm then began to take a northward track the next day, passing the western tip of Cuba while gaining strength. On August 29th, Idalia was upgraded to a Category 1 hurricane early in the morning, then intensified to a Category 2 hurricane later in the day while tracking across the southeast Gulf of Mexico. Idalia then continued to strengthen as it accelerated northward on August 30th, passing off the Florida Suncoast as a Category 2 hurricane, before rapidly intensifying to a major Category 4 hurricane while approaching the Big Ben region of Florida across the northeast Gulf of Mexico. Idalia then made landfall at 645 AM EST on August 30th about 20 miles south of Perry, Florida as a Category 3 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 125 mph and a minimum central pressure of 949 mb. ||Idalia continued to track north-northeast after landfall, eventually turning northeast and weakening to a strong tropical storm while traversing southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina late morning through evening hours on August 30th. Minimum surface pressures of 985.4 mb at Hinesville, GA (KLHW), 984.6 mb at Charleston City, SC (CHLS1) and 983.3 mb at the Savannah Entrance Light across nearshore coastal waters were recorded as Idalia tracked across the local area. Idalia then continued tracking northeast away from the region, exiting into the western Atlantic just south of Myrtle Beach, SC during early morning hours on August 31st. Idalia then began an eastward path across the western Atlantic, becoming a post tropical cyclone by late day, before continuing a track toward Bermuda for the next couple days. ||Across southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina, the main impacts associated with Idalia included tropical storm force winds, heavy rain, storm surge and tornadoes. Tropical storm force winds gusts up to 40 to 69 mph (highest near coastal areas) aided with heavy rains led to numerous trees and power lines down across southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina. On August 30th, a maximum sustained wind of 44 knots and peak wind gust of 60 knots was recorded at the Tybee Island South sensor (XTYE) in southeast Georgia while a maximum sustained wind of 41 knots was recorded at the Folly South End (XFSE) sensor and a peak wind gust of 58 knots was recorded at the Beaufort (XBUF) sensor in southeast South Carolina. Additionally, a maximum sustained wind of 49 knots and a peak wind gust of 60 knots was recorded at the Savannah Entrance Light (XSEL) across nearshore coastal waters. One indirect injury occurred due to tropical storm winds when a vehicle collided with a fallen tree in Effingham County, GA. No fatalities occurred due to tropical storm winds across the area.||Storm total rainfall amounts generally ranged between 1 to 2 inches across coastal areas of southeast Georgia, 2 to 4 inches along and east of Interstate 95 across southeast South Carolina and 4 to 9 inches across far inland areas of southeast Georgia and areas west of Interstate 95 in southeast South Carolina. A peak storm total rainfall of 9.05 inches was recorded near Smoaks, South Carolina while a peak storm total rainfall of 8.28 inches was recorded near Metter, Georgia. Heavy rains across inland areas led to instances of flash flooding with numerous roads washed out, water entering a few structures and 2 vehicles being swept off roadways. No injuries or fatalities occurred due to heavy rain/flash flooding across the area.||Idalia's passage was coincident with high tide, resulting in storm surge generally between 2 to 3.5 ft along the southeast South Carolina coast. A maximum tide level of 3.47 ft MHHW (9.23 ft MLLW) was observed at the Charleston Harbor (CHTS1) tide gauge at 718 PM EST on August 30th, making it the 5th highest tide on record for that location. Damage/inundation from storm surge crossing roads, entering properties and flooding structures was most notable along the Charleston, Colleton, and Beaufort County coasts, mainly in the McClellanville, Isle of Palms, Mount Pleasant, Folly Beach, Downtown Charleston, Edisto Island and Saint Helena Island communities/areas. Peak storm surge (3.5 ft) was noted along areas adjacent to the Ashley River and the Charleston Harbor in Charleston County. Further south, a maximum tide level of 1.95 ft MHHW (9.45 ft MLLW) was observed at the Fort Pulaski (FPKG1) tide gauge at 654 PM EST on August 29th, which was consistent with water levels that typically do not produce significant impacts along the southeast Georgia coast. No injuries or fatalities occurred due to storm surge across the area.||A total of 6 tropical related tornadoes occurred across southeast Georgia into southeast South Carolina within rainbands associated with Idalia. One short-lived EF0 tornado occurred in Liberty County across southeast Georgia, mainly producing tree damage. Another EF0 tornado occurred in Charleston County across southeast South Carolina, downing/uprooting trees and producing minor roof damage to homes and vehicles in Mount Pleasant. Two waterspouts also shifted onshore along the northern end of Folly Beach in Charleston County, but were short-lived and caused no discernable damage. Two tornadoes occurred in Berkeley County across southeast South Carolina, one being an EF1 tornado that snapped/uprooted numerous trees along its path in the Francis Marion Forest and the second being a short-lived EF0 tornado that flipped a vehicle over on a highly traveled road in Goose Creek, SC. Two injuries resulted from the flipped vehicle. No fatalities occurred due to tornadoes across the area.

episodes.185220: Lingering moisture extending across South Florida from Hurricane Idalia well to the NE of the region led to the formation of afternoon showers and thunderstorms with heavy rainfall and gusty winds across SE Florida.
episodes.185354: Tropical storm Idalia, which tracked east-northeast off the North Carolina coast, brought several inches of rainfall to central North Carolina. Isolated flash flooding was reported in Sampson County.

events.narrative: Dorchester County Emergency Management provided pictures of a paved road damaged near the intersection of Durhams Corner Road and McAlhany Road and near Durham's Store due to heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Storm Idalia. The roadbed under the eastbound lane near a small creek was severely eroded and compromised. Emergency management also reported unpaved Westfield Road washed out near the intersection with Mulberry Road.

Colleton County Emergency Management provided pictures of roadway damage on Cayce Road not far from the intersection with Broxton Bridge Highway due to heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Storm Idalia. The culvert pipe failed and more than half of that portion of the roadway collapsed.
A Colleton County emergency manager reported a portion of unpaved See See Road washed out near the Ashepoo River due to heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Storm Idalia.
The Jordan E. Mesonet site (MTM88) measured a 59 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
Orangeburg County Emergency Manager reported multiple flooded and impassable roads in and around Holly Hill. 6 inches of water covering roadways.
Orangeburg County Emergency Manager reported several roads in and around Bowman impassable due to flooding, including Poplar Road, Canal Street and Bowman Avenue.
Orangeburg County Emergency Manager reported multiple roads impassable due to flooding in and around Santee.
Orangeburg County Emergency Manager reported roadways impassable due to flooding from the intersection of Branchdale and Eutaw Highways to the train tracks near Factory Road.
Streets around the Weldon Auditorium including Old Georgetown Road closed due to flooding.
The King Coulee RAWS site (KIGM8) measured a 59 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
Heavy rain of 1-1.5 in less than one hour caused Robb Wash to flow 2-3 feet deep across Pima Rd.
A supercell thunderstorm passed through the Arnegard and surrounding areas, resulting in an extended period of large hail. The largest hail was the size of golf balls. Vehicles were damaged.
The public reported tree branches being knocked down.  They estimated the wind was gusting up to 60 mph.
Tree damage was reported. A tree was snapped off at the base and uprooted. Multiple 4-12 inch diameter branches were broken.
An 18 inch diameter, dead tree was snapped.
The BLM Terry Mesonet site (MTM29) measured a 58 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
At 1845MST, thunderstorm wind gusts to 59 mph were measured near Prospect and Larkspur CW8733 and near Old Spanish Trail and Melpomene Way FW3746.
The Glendive Airport ASOS (KGDV) measured a 58 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
The BLM Glendive Mesonet site (MTM28) measured a 58 mph thunderstorm wind gust.

Waterspout was observed moving ashore near Ocean Blvd. and 56th|Avenue North. It tracked north-northwest causing sporadic damage|to homes in the Cherry Grove area. It then crossed Williams Creek|into the Tidewater Golf Club, downing a few trees and numerous|large limbs. There were likely a few brief spin-ups in the|vicinity of the waterspout as it came ashore.
SCDOT reports Isaac Gerald Rd. to Garner Rd. is closed due to flooding. Time estimated via crest unit stream flow maximum.
Multiple vehicles were damaged.
WMBF reports flooding with fast moving water along Highway 501 near Main St. in Aynor.
The public estimated thunderstorm wind gusts at around 60 mph.  They also reported hail up to the size of peas, along with some minor street flooding.
Thunderstorm wind gusts were estimated by a trained spotter.
SCDOT reports all lanes are closed from Hunting Swamp to Elbow Road near Conway, SC due to flooding. Time estimated via crest unit stream flow maximum.
SCDOT reports that all lanes are blocked from Walnut Street to S-151 near Loris, SC. Time estimated via crest unit streamflow maximum.

An USGS automated rain gages, located in the nearby village of Dededo, reported 2.10 inches in one hour from 1445ChST to 1545ChST.  Photos and videos shared to the office around 1700ChST showed the worse of the flooding occurred in low lying areas near Harmon Industrial Road and Illipog Drive, located in the village of Harmon. One photo shows a parked four door sedan with water above all four tires of the car and just reaching up to just above the bottom of the tail lights, putting most of the license just under the water. Using a similar sedan as reference the estimated height of the water was between 2 and 3 feet. Water looked to ponding to that area in the photo, with the car located in the lowest spot of alley branching off of Illipog Drive.  Total rainfall reported by the Dededo rain guage from 1445ChST to 1745ChST was 2.72 inches. Based on the water level around the car, it possible the car would need to be towed and have maintenance done to the car's interior and engine to prevent water damage to the engine and the growth of mold in the car, so damages was roughly estimated to be around 1 Thousand $USD.

A video taken from a truck and sent to the WFO around 1710ChST showed water flowing across Gayinero Road in the village of Yigo. Water was coving the entire road, and rough estimates based on objects next to the road suggest water is at least a couple of inches deep and was rapidly flowed towards a ditch or drop off on the side of the road. The nearby USGS Mt. Santa Rosa rain gage reported 2.28 inches of rain between 1445ChST and 1645ChST. The heaviest rain fell between 1500ChST and 1600ChST with a hourly rain rate of 1.74 inches. No damage was reported.
Reports high water and a tree across the road along Progressive Farm Rd. near Bloomingdale Rd. south of Fairmont, NC. Time estimated via crest unit streamflow maximum.
Reports that Gores Trailer Rd. is closed due to standing water at Pineland Woods Dr. near Whiteville, NC. Time estimated via crest unit streamflow maximum.
Reports that us-701 is closed at Richard Wright Road in Tabor City, NC. Time estimated via radar and crest.
Reports NC-410 from US-74 business to East Railroad Ave. in Chadbourn, NC.
Carteret County 911 reported street flooding in Atlantic Beach at the intersection of HWY 58 and the Atlantic Beach Causeway.
Reports that Scott Road is closed due to high water between Highsmith Road and Highway 210. Time estimated via crest unit streamflow maximum.
Water covered the roads at the intersection of Joslyn Dr. and Country Club Rd. The time was based on radar.
A Candler County emergency manager reported a 55 acre pond dam failed on Cook Pond Road due to recent heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Storm Idalia.

A Dorchester County emergency manager reported 2 vehicles swept off the road by moving floodwaters on Indian Field Circle near Highway 15 due to recent heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Storm Idalia. Both drivers were able to escape their vehicles with no injuries.
Lighthouse Road was flooded. The COOP observer measured 8.47 inches of rain at this location. The time was estimated based on radar.
Several roads were impassable due to flooding within the city of Jacksonville. Some vehicles were disabled due to flooding as well.
Pinewood Circle was flooded in Pine Knoll Shores.
Golden Farm Rd. was completely flooded in Otway.
A few roads were closed in the Pink Hill area due to flooding.
A few roads were closed in the Kinston area due to flooding.
A few roads were closed in the La Grange area due to flooding.
Onslow Drive, between Eastwood Drive and Highway 17, was closed due to flooding.
Highway 17 North southbound from Parkway to Montford was barricaded due to water covering the road.
Moosehaven Road was closed near Highway 17.
McDaniel Drive through Kensington Drive was closed due to flooding.
Indian Drive and Cardinal Road were closed due to flooding.
Public reported about 10 inches of water covering Howard Street in Ocracoke. The time was based on radar.
A fire marshal reported a flooded roadway near the 900 block of Wildcat Rd.
A fire marshal reported that Highway 41 was flooded near Clear Run.
The National Park Service reported all four campgrounds were closed at the Cape Point Campground due to flooding.
Fourteen roads were closed throughout Duplin County due to high water covering them.
High water covered NC-12 between Frisco and Hatteras Village.
Beacon Drive in Rodanthe was flooded from standing rain water.
Flood waters affected a car in the street next to Urb Altamira between San Juan and Guaynabo.
WeatherSTEM site in Hobe Sound measured a 34 knot wind gust from the south-southwest.

Standing water was reported along several streets in Miami Beach from heavy rainfall during the late afternoon and early evening. As much as 3 inches of rain was estimated to have fallen in a short period of time.
One to 1.5 inch diameter hail was reported in the Payson area between 330 and 345 PM MST.
Thunderstorm winds blew over a big rig and blew down power lines.
